title: Mouse-wheel zoom discards ~99% of scroll events - 172 notches move the FOV from 60 to 29 degrees
what_happened: Each wheel notch is supposed to zoom 1.15-1.2x. Measured live: 5 notches spaced 2.0s apart took FOV 28.9 -> 14.4 deg (exactly 1.15^5, correct). 12 notches spaced 0.3s took 60.0 -> 41.7 deg (the effect of ~2.6 notches). 120 notches spaced 0.05s took 34.7 -> 28.9 deg (the effect of ~1.3 notches out of 120). Spinning the wheel at any natural speed therefore barely zooms; it took 172 notches over two minutes to get from the default 60 deg to 28.9 deg, and there is no other zoom control on the desktop layout (no +/- buttons, no FOV field, and the '=' / '-' hotkeys are dead - see the focus finding).
expected: Successive wheel events must compound onto the pending zoom target, not restart the animation from the current (barely-moved) FOV. A user should reach an imaging FOV in a few flicks of the wheel.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > point at the sky > spin the wheel up 20 notches quickly, watch 'FOV (short axis)' in the bottom bar.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-28.png (41.7 after 12 notches), -29.png (34.7 after 40 more), -31.png (28.9 after 120 more), -36.png (14.4 after 5 slow notches). Source: _animateZoom sets _startFOV = current provider FOV and calls _zoomController.forward(from:0) on every event - packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/widgets/interactive_sky_view.dart:475-485,660-668
proposed_fix: Accumulate into _targetFOV (use the in-flight target, not the current FOV, as the base) so N rapid notches equal N steps.
verdict_reasoning: Measured myself. 20 xdotool wheel-up notches at 50 ms spacing over the sky canvas moved FOV 60.0 -> exactly 50.0, i.e. 60/1.2 - the effect of ONE notch out of twenty (95% discarded). Then 5 notches at 2.0 s spacing moved 50.0 -> 21.9, exactly the fully compounded 50/1.2^3/1.15^2 = 21.88, so slow notches apply in full. Code confirms the mechanism at the cited line: interactive_sky_view.dart:475 _animateZoom sets _startFOV from the provider's current (barely-moved) fieldOfView and calls _zoomController.forward(from: 0.0) at :484 on every scroll event (:660-668), restarting the 300 ms easeOutCubic instead of compounding onto the pending target. Location interactive_sky_view.dart:475 is exact. One sub-claim inside the finding is now false: the '=' / '-' hotkeys are NOT dead, so a working keyboard zoom exists - which is why I leave it at P2 rather than raising it.

title: Planetarium opens centred on RA 0h/Dec 0 - 25 degrees below the horizon at the configured site
what_happened: Opening Plan Tonight > Planetarium for the first time shows 'Center RA: 0h 0m 0s, Center Dec: +0 0'' and the on-screen alt/az HUD reads az 293 deg, alt -25 deg. The default view is pointed a quarter of the way down into the ground. The same bug was already found and fixed for the RESET action (the code comment in _resetView says so), but the initial view state was left at 0,0.
expected: First paint should use the same home centre the reset action uses (skyViewHomeCenterProvider = zenith), so the user opens on sky that is actually up.
repro: Settings > Location > set lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium. Read the bottom bar and the compass HUD.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/r-planetarium-09.png - 'Center RA: 0h 0m 0s  Center Dec: +0 0'  FOV 60.0' with the compass rose showing 293 deg and the altitude gauge showing -25 deg; independently computed alt/az for RA 0/Dec 0 at 40N/105W at 18:30:10Z is alt -24.6, az 292.6.
location_wrong: Cited planetarium_screen.dart with no line, and the value is not set there. The default lives in packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/sky_view.dart:8-9, `SkyViewNotifier() : super(const SkyViewState(centerRA: 0, centerDec: 0, fieldOfView: 60))`. The home value it should adopt is skyViewHomeCenterProvider, same file :309.
proposed_fix: Initialise skyViewStateProvider's centre from skyViewHomeCenterProvider on first build.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a fresh profile. Set the site to lat 40 / lon -105 / 1650 m, opened Plan Tonight > Planetarium: bottom bar reads 'Center RA: 0h 0m 0s  Center Dec: +0 0'  FOV 60.0' and the compass HUD reads az 328 / alt -45 (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-08.png). Independently recomputed: at LST 10.54 h, RA 0/Dec 0 has HA 158.15 deg so alt = asin(cos40*cos158.15) = -45.3 deg - the HUD is right and the default view really points into the ground. (My alt differs from the finding's -25 deg only because the audit ran at a different clock time; same defect.) The reset action was fixed - pressing 'h' goes to the zenith - but the initial state was not.

title: Moon is always drawn full and always labelled 'MOON 100%' - percent is fed into a 0-1 fraction and clamped
what_happened: On 2026-08-02 14:26:36 UTC from 40N/105W the planetarium drew the Moon as a solid, fully-lit white disc with the label 'MOON 100%'. The true illuminated fraction at that instant is 84.6% (independent Meeus computation, elongation 133.7 deg), and the app's own Dashboard Moon card says 'Waning Gibbous 84% illuminated' while Plan Tonight's target card says 'Moon is 79% illuminated'. Three surfaces, three different numbers, and the planetarium's is the one that is impossible. Root cause is a unit mismatch: AstronomyCalculations.moonIllumination() returns a PERCENT (0-100) and its doc comment says so, but SkyRenderer._drawMoon documents its third tuple element as 'illuminated fraction (0 = new, 1 = full)' and does rawIllumination.clamp(0.0, 1.0). Any real phase above 1% therefore clamps to exactly 1.0, so both the terminator geometry and the label are pinned at full moon for 29 of every 29.5 days. Only within a few hours of new moon does the value fall below 1 and render anything else - and then it renders a 1%-lit crescent as if it were 100%-scaled.
expected: The label should read the real illuminated percentage (84% here) and the disc should be drawn with the corresponding terminator, matching the Dashboard's Moon card.
repro: Settings > Location > lat 40, lon -105 > Plan Tonight > Planetarium. The Moon glyph is near the default 0h/0deg view. Read its label; then compare with Dashboard > Moon card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-10.png (full white disc, label 'MOON 100%'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-02.png (Dashboard: 'Waning Gibbous 84% illuminated'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-07.png (Plan Tonight: 'Moon is 79% illuminated'). Source: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/astronomy_calculations.dart:761-785 returns 0-100; packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/rendering/sky_renderer/solar_system_and_markers.dart:481-486 clamps to 0..1 and :571 does (illumination * 100).round().
location_wrong: Cited solar_system_and_markers.dart:481 is the `if (moonPosition == null) return;` guard; the clamp is :484-486 and the label :571. The upstream unit error is at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/widgets/interactive_sky_view.dart:1026, with the same feed duplicated in planetarium_screen/actions.dart:212 and widgets/view_controls.dart:396 - editing only :481 misses three call sites.
proposed_fix: Divide by 100 at the three call sites that build the moonPosition tuple (interactive_sky_view.dart:1026, planetarium_screen/actions.dart:212, widgets/view_controls.dart:396 - the exported finder chart is affected too), or better, change moonIllumination() to return a fraction and fix the one place that formats it as a percent.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on the rebuilt bundle at 2026-08-03 20:43 UTC / 40N 105W: the chart draws a solid white disc labelled 'MOON 100%' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-08.png, again at v2p-21.png). My own Meeus computation gives 73.7% illuminated at that instant, and the app's own Dashboard Moon card says 'Waning Gibbous 74% illuminated' - so 74% is what the app computes elsewhere and 100% is the renderer's. Chain confirmed in code: astronomy_calculations.dart:844-868 moonIllumination returns (1+cos)/2*100 i.e. a PERCENT; interactive_sky_view.dart:1026 passes moonIllumination.illumination into the third tuple slot; solar_system_and_markers.dart:484-486 does rawIllumination.clamp(0.0,1.0) and :571 does (illumination*100).round(). Anything above 1% pins to 1.0.

title: The command bar's 'Search' button (and its Ctrl/Cmd+K shortcut) never focuses the search field, and does not even switch the panel to the Search tab
what_happened: With the right-hand plan panel already open on the Info tab, clicking the command bar's 'Search  ⌘K' button only showed a 'Search the sky' tooltip: the panel stayed on the Info tab and the caret was not placed in 'Search objects, names...'. Typing 'Albireo' immediately after produced nothing in the field. Selecting the Search tab by hand left the field still unfocused - typing 'Albireo' again produced nothing, the panel kept showing its 'Search for objects / Try "M42", "Andromeda Galaxy", or "Sirius"' empty state. Ctrl+K and Super+K also did nothing. Source: the handler is _openPlanPanelOnSearch, which on desktop sets _planPanelOpen = true and _layersPanelOpen = false and stops - it never selects the search tab and never requests focus for the text field.
expected: A control labelled Search with a keyboard-shortcut badge should open the panel ON the search tab with the caret in the field, so the user can type immediately. Finding an object by name is the single most common thing anyone does in a planetarium; it currently takes three separate clicks (open panel, Search tab, click into the field) before the first keystroke.
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > open the right sidebar and select any tab except Search > click the 'Search  ⌘K' button in the command bar > type 'Albireo'. Nothing is entered. Repeat after clicking the Search tab: still nothing.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-27.png (tooltip shown, panel unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-28.png (still on Info tab, field empty after typing 'Albireo'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-29.png (Search tab selected by hand, field still empty after typing 'Albireo'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-30.png (empty after Ctrl+K + 'M42'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-31.png (empty after Super+K + 'M42'). Source: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/planetarium/widgets/redesign/planetarium_shell.dart:437-447.
location_wrong: Cited planetarium_shell.dart:443; the method begins at :445 and the empty desktop branch is :451-454. Two-line drift, file correct.
proposed_fix: In _openPlanPanelOnSearch also set the panel's selected tab to Search and call requestFocus() on the search field's FocusNode (autofocus on the field when the tab is entered from this path).
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live. Clicking the command bar's 'Search K' entry opened the right plan panel on the TONIGHT tab, and typing 'M57' immediately after entered nothing anywhere (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-14.png: the panel shows Evening Twilight, the field still shows its placeholder). Code matches: planetarium_shell.dart:445-455 _openPlanPanelOnSearch sets only _planPanelOpen = true and _layersPanelOpen = false on desktop - no tab selection, no requestFocus; actions.dart:512-518 routes Ctrl/Cmd+K to the same method. Clicking the field by hand does work, so search itself is fine and this is ergonomics - P2 stands.

title: Planets are computed for the equinox of date but stars and DSOs are drawn at J2000 - the two are mixed on one chart, so planets sit ~22 arcmin off the star background
what_happened: Clicking Jupiter on the chart at 2026-08-02 15:12 UTC from 40N/105W gave RA 8h 39m 30.9s, Dec +18d 53' 53", Alt 38.1, Az 96.9. An independent Keplerian ephemeris puts Jupiter at J2000 RA 8h37m58.3s / +18d59'31"; precessing that to the equinox of date gives 8h39m29.5s / +18d53'50", which matches the app to 1.4 s of RA and 3 arcsec of declination, and its alt/az (38.11 / 96.94) matches the app's to 0.01 deg - whereas the J2000 position gives 38.46 / 97.12, which does not. So the planet path precesses. The star path does not: the app reports Deneb as 20h 41m 25.9s / +45d 16' 49", which is its J2000 position to the tenth of a second, and its Alt/Az reproduces from those unprecessed coordinates. Both sets of coordinates are then fed to the same projection, so every planet is drawn displaced from the true stellar background by the accumulated precession since J2000 - about 1m32s of RA and 5.7 arcmin of declination here, roughly 22 arcmin total, or two-thirds of a Moon diameter. The screenshot shows this in the worst possible place: Jupiter is drawn right next to M44, the Beehive, and the drawn Jupiter-M44 separation is wrong by that amount.
expected: One reference frame for everything on the chart. Either precess the catalog to the epoch of observation before projecting (correct, and it also fixes the alt/az error already filed), or express the planetary ephemeris in J2000. Mixing them is worse than either.
repro: Settings > Location 40N 105W > Plan Tonight > Planetarium > press the home/reset icon so the zenith is centred > click Jupiter and read its Coordinates, then click a bright star and read its Coordinates. The planet is equinox-of-date, the star is J2000.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-66.png (Jupiter: RA 8h 39m 30.9s, Dec +18 53' 53", Alt 38.1, Az 96.9, drawn beside 'M44 - Beehive'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-26.png (Deneb: RA 20h 41m 25.9s, Dec +45 16' 49" = J2000 exactly). Computation: J2000 Jupiter 8h37m58.3s/+18d59'31"; precessed 8h39m29.5s/+18d53'50"; alt/az from precessed 38.11/96.94 vs from J2000 38.46/97.12.
location_wrong: Cited astronomy_calculations.dart. The planet frame is set in a DIFFERENT file: packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/astronomy/planetary_positions.dart:145-153. astronomy_calculations.dart is only relevant as the home of the unused precessFromJ2000ToDate (:442).
proposed_fix: Precess catalogue positions to the observation epoch inside the render pipeline (a single rotation applied to the star/DSO arrays per frame or per minute), so planets, stars, the grid and the horizon transform all share one equinox.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced against an independent ephemeris. Clicked Saturn at 2026-08-03 20:51:39 UTC: app reports RA 0h58m00.4s / Dec +3 26' 07". My own Keplerian ephemeris (JPL approximate elements, light-time corrected) gives J2000 geocentric 0h56m56.9s / +3 19' 59" and equinox-of-date 0h58m19.2s / +3 28' 35". The app sits ~4.7 arcmin from the of-date value and ~20 arcmin from J2000 - unambiguously equinox of date (residual within the app's truncated-VSOP and my Keplerian error budget for Saturn). In the same session Vega read out at its exact J2000 position. So the two families are in different frames on one chart; the offset at Saturn is 82 s of RA plus 8.6 arcmin of Dec, ~22 arcmin, matching the claim. I also saw the exact scenario the finding describes - Jupiter drawn right beside M44 (v2p-26.png). Code: planetary_positions.dart:145-153 converts VSOP-of-date ecliptic coordinates with the obliquity OF DATE while the star catalogue is J2000 and precessFromJ2000ToDate is never called.

title: Planets are typed as 'Star' in the object popup and written to the observation log that way, and the popup shows the internal id 'PLANET_Jupiter'
what_happened: Clicking Jupiter opens a popup headed 'Jupiter' with an identifier chip reading 'PLANET_Jupiter', 'mag -1.8' and a 'Type' field that says 'Star'. Logging an observation from that popup persists the same mistake: the row written to observation_logs is (object_name 'Jupiter', object_type 'star', catalog_id 'PLANET_Jupiter', ra 8.65857 h, dec 18.898, altitude 38.68, azimuth 97.48, rating 3, seeing good, transparency good, latitude 40, longitude -105). So the app's permanent observing record classifies a planet as a star, and the user-visible catalogue identifier is an internal enum token rather than a designation anyone would recognise.
expected: Type should read 'Planet' and the chip should show something meaningful (or nothing) rather than the internal key. object_type in observation_logs should be 'planet' so the log can later be filtered or exported (an observing log is data the user keeps for years).
repro: Plan Tonight > Planetarium > press home to centre the zenith > click Jupiter. Read the Type row and the chip. Then Log Observation > Log Observation, and read the observation_logs table.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-67.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/rp2-69.png (popup: 'Jupiter', chip 'PLANET_Jupiter', 'Type: Star'). DB after saving: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/r-planetarium/data/skotiq.db 'select * from observation_logs' -> 1|1785683758|Jupiter|star|PLANET_Jupiter|8.65857259173372|18.8980441804957|38.6778254522709|97.4768462200507||3||good|good||40.0|-105.0
location_wrong: object_info_popup.dart is right for the Type row (:429-434, heading/chip :343) but is only half of it. The persisted 'star' comes from the Star typing upstream at packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/widgets/interactive_sky_view.dart:1199 and packages/skotiq_planetarium/lib/src/providers/planetarium_providers/object_search.dart:276.
proposed_fix: Map the synthetic planet objects to a 'planet' object type at the point they are constructed, and hide/replace the PLANET_* catalog id in the popup chip.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on Saturn (Jupiter was below the horizon at audit time; identical code path). Popup heading 'Saturn', identifier chip 'PLANET_Saturn', 'mag 0.8', 'Type: Star' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/v2p-22.png). Pressed Log Observation -> Log Observation and read the scratch DB myself: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/v2-planetarium/data/skotiq.db 'select * from observation_logs' returns 1|1785790395|Saturn|star|PLANET_Saturn|0.9667802|3.4351809|-36.513|315.933||3||good|good||40.0|-105.0 - object_type is literally 'star', catalog_id is the internal token. Mechanism: interactive_sky_view.dart:1199 and object_search.dart:276 construct planets as Star(id: 'PLANET_<name>'), so object_info_popup.dart:429-434 `if (obj is Star) typeLabel = 'Star'` fires. search_header.dart:454-459 already has an isPlanet prefix helper for the search list, so the popup and the logger are the surfaces that never got it.
